Duplicated clip helper: `_clip_run` (skills/ultrapowers/scripts/compile_plan.py, new block ~line 2698) reimplements the compiler's existing `_short(s, n=80)` (same file, line 537) exactly — collapse whitespace, return as-is under the cap, else `s[:n-1] + "…"`. The docstring's justification ("the command, not its marker, so nothing is stripped off the front") is true of the advisory-section `_clip` (line 2651, which strips a bullet marker) but not of `_short`, which strips nothing off the front. `RUN_CLIP = 80` plus `_short(command, RUN_CLIP)` would give byte-identical output for both the short and the clipped case that the exam pins (`test_run_chained_semicolon_detail_names_the_command_and_the_join`, `..._clips_a_long_command`) with one fewer helper. Not blocking: the behaviour is correct and matches M2's "first 80 characters" in the repo's own `_short` idiom.; Undisclosed narrowing of M2 for two species: `_species_universal_as_count_floor` and `_species_duration_without_clock` both `continue` when a clause has no citing legs (`if not ... or not cited`), while M2 reads "all of whose citing legs contain `at least`" / "none of whose citing legs contains `elapsed`…", which are vacuously true for zero legs. `_species_default_unpinned` carries a comment explaining exactly this guard ("An UNCITED clause is already a citation-grammar refusal"); the other two carry the guard with no comment. The divergence is inert — `clause_citation_violations` (compile_plan.py:564-567) already refuses `grammar: Machine clause M<n> has no citing Proof leg`, so no plan reaching the render can hold an uncited clause — so this is a comment fix, not a behaviour fix: extend the existing rationale comment to cover all three species.; Three species narrow M2 by an undisclosed-in-the-exam guard: `_species_default_unpinned` (compile_plan.py, `if m and cited and not any(...)`), `_species_universal_as_count_floor` and `_species_duration_without_clock` all `continue` when a clause has NO citing leg. M2 as written is vacuously true there — "whose citing legs' text nowhere contains that literal", "all of whose citing legs contain `at least`", "none of whose citing legs contains `elapsed`…" all hold over an empty set, so the letter of the spec fires and the code stays silent. The code comment discloses the reasoning (an uncited clause is already a `grammar:` refusal from `clause_citation_violations`, compile_plan.py:564-567), and on a plan that compiles the case is unreachable — but `render_advisories` still runs over a plan the check REFUSED (only malformed headings / duplicate ids abort it early), which is exactly when an author is repairing. The divergence is defensible and I would keep it; what is missing is a leg pinning it. Add one leg to `tests/test_compile_plan_proof_species.py` — a clause with no citing leg (the plan exits 2) drawing no `default-unpinned`/`universal-as-count-floor`/`duration-without-clock` line — so the narrowing is graded rather than incidental.; `_clip_run` (compile_plan.py, new) re-implements `_short` (compile_plan.py:537) — same whitespace collapse, same `n-1` + `…` clip — differing only by an `.rstrip()` before the ellipsis, and it is now the third clipper in the file beside `_short` and `_clip`. `_short(command, RUN_CLIP)` would do the job; if the trailing-space trim matters, add `.rstrip()` to `_short` (it changes no existing output, since `_short` already collapses runs of whitespace to single spaces) and drop `_clip_run` and `RUN_CLIP`'s private twin. The exam's `test_run_chained_semicolon_detail_clips_a_long_command` grades the observable clip either way.
